newsitem.title: UK: London freight market sees steady to rising rates.
newsitem.headline: London freight market sees steady to rising rates.

text.p: Panamax rates were at least steady or slowly rising in most areas and many brokers thought they were likely to continue edging up.

According to one broker, caper activity was 'taking a breather' in the Atlantic but showing more signs of life in the east. Handy-size business was still sluggish generally. The BFI rose 4 points to 1,266.

GRAIN - Grain houses found themselves competing with minerals charterers in a lively Panamax market in the US Gulf. Although reported fixtures remained mostly steady, brokers expected rates to appreciate gradually for June/early July positions in the Atlantic and Pacific grain trades.

Egyptian charterers were said to have two more early Panamax grain cargoes to cover from US Gulf, and some believed S Korean charterers have yet to quote their first half July requirements Us Gulf/Far East. Continental remained open for an early vessel US Gulf/Egypt, having failed with the 1971-built Angelic Grace 68,847 dwt delivery US Gulf at close to $7,250 daily plus $125,000 bonus on account of the vessel's age.

Cargill took June Panamax tonnage for heavy grain US Gulf/Continent (Maritime Wisdom 63,600 tonnes) and US Gulf/Egypt (Mercury Star 55,000/5 tonnes) at unremarkable rates of $11.00 and $12.50 respectively basis. There was speculation among brokers that Cargill might not find it easy to fix its June 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan at $21.00 no combo and might have to concede a little more. It was not clear if Continental still wanted tonnage from US Gulf as well as NOPAC to Japan. Toshuka were said to have fixed Halla tonnage for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan at $20.85 no combo for August.

June tonnage was tight in S America where Seatrans was reported to have paid a hefty close to $12,250 daily plus $225,000 bonus for the Glencore-relet Oinoussian Seaman 64,000 dwt delivery Paranagua Triphina. Athiniotissa 64,060 dwt spot Recalada and Sun P 65,738 dwt spot Lisbon were also said to have been fixed for S American grain but details were not available.

In a quiet day for fresh business Cargill had an enquiry for a vessel of 2.7/3.2m cft up river and Brazil/Lisbon-Hamburg range for 27 June/10 July, and Toepfer quoted 1.3/1.5m cft Mississippi/Italy 20/27 June.

MINERALS - Although the Pacific caper market was healthier for owners, Atlantic rates appeared to be falling. Alassini Avra was booked by GKE for 110,000/10 coal Hampton Roads/Rotterdam for mid July at only $5.60, compared with Hoogovens' fixture of Wah Shan for 120,000/10 to Ijmuiden reported a week ago at $6.20.

Panamax rates moved in the opposite direction. The 1981-built Anna 65,000 dwt which failed on subjects with Cosco Usec/China at $10,750 daily plus $150,000 bonus was understood booked by Transfield Us Gulf/China with fertilisers at $11,000 daily plus $200,000 bonus. Cosco was said to be working Lea 69,447 dwt US Gulf/China at $11,400 daily plus $160,000 bonus, against $11,600 and $170,000. Elsewhere Safmarine was said to be working World Spear 67,000 dwt for 2 laden legs to the continent, and NSAC was linked with Linda Oldendorff 75,100 dwt on subjects delivery prompt Yantai for 2 laden legs Nopac/Bin Qasim and S Africa/continent at about $6,500/7,000 daily for the 1st 50 days and $9,500 daily for the balance.

Details of EMC's panamax coal fixture Richard's bay/Dunkirk remained private. Showa booked a modern panamax from the Far East for an Australian round on private terms and the 1982-built captain George Tsangaris 61,349 dwt was rumoured to have failed on subjects with transfield Australia/China at $7,950 daily plus $110,000 bonus.
